title: Oracle says its OpenAI contract is fully funded and pre-empts media reports
excerpt: ‘Any media reports that will come out and say the contrary are incorrect and wrong,’ Oracle said of its OpenAI contract funding.
content_html:
Oracle says it has secured all the funding it needs to fulfil its infrastructure contract with OpenAI. The company made the claim in a post on X on Friday. It also pushed back in advance against any coverage that says otherwise.

“Any media reports that will come out and say the contrary are incorrect and wrong,” Oracle wrote.

Oracle has secured all the funding we need to fulfill our contract with OpenAI. With our final capital raise earlier this month, we became the first hyperscaler fully funded for this investment cycle. The financing we outlined at Oracle Investor Day, including vendor financing, is in place. Any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options. Our ability to deliver on our OpenAI contract does not depend on those discussions. Any media reports that will come out and say the contrary are incorrect and wrong.

Oracle and OpenAI are making rapid progress on our infrastructure partnership. Our Abilene campus, where Astra-6 was trained, is nearly complete. Shackelford, our next gigawatt-scale campus, is fully permitted. The handover of NVIDIA Vera Rubin racks in its data halls is on track for the coming weeks.

We continue to expect positive free cash flow in the second half of FY2028. We are targeting more than $30 billion in free cash flow in FY2029 and expect to self-fund future growth beginning that year.

— Oracle (@Oracle) November 20, 2026


Oracle did not say which reports it had in mind. The post went up at 4:01pm New York time, a minute after US markets closed. Its shares rose as much as 3.3% in after-hours trading, Reuters reported.

What Oracle says is in place

The company tied the funding to its final capital raise earlier this month, the $20bn debt and equity sale. With it, Oracle said, it became the first hyperscaler fully funded for this investment cycle.

The financing it set out at its Investor Day, including vendor financing, is in place, Oracle said. It described any further private talks with vendors as extra options and said its OpenAI contract does not depend on them.

The post also gave an update on the build. Oracle said its campus in Abilene, Texas, where OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra model was trained, is nearly complete. Its next gigawatt-scale campus, in Shackelford County, Texas, is fully permitted. Oracle expects Nvidia’s Vera Rubin racks to arrive in its data halls there in the coming weeks.

Oracle and OpenAI plan 4.5 gigawatts of extra US capacity on top of the first Stargate site in Abilene, Reuters reported.

The cash flow promise

Oracle repeated its forecast of positive free cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028. It is targeting more than $30bn in free cash flow in fiscal 2029. From that year, it expects to fund its own growth.

A second post followed with a standard disclaimer. It said the statements about Oracle’s plans are forward-looking, carry material risks and uncertainties, and could differ from actual results.

Investors have questioned how much capital Oracle needs for its AI data centre expansion and how exposed it is to OpenAI, Reuters reported. Oracle’s data centre spending already outpaces its quarterly revenue. Earlier this month, Microsoft began winding down its deal to rent AI computing from Oracle.
